EXECUTED ANALYSIS COMPLETE (deterministic: re-run reproduces identical table checksums).

## Headline result (Q8_ML_Addressing_* multi-select, n = 194 respondents with a valid Q8 block)

| rank | role | count/n | % | bootstrap SE (pp) | 95% CI percentile | 95% CI BCa | 95% CI Wilson | P(rank 1) | P(top 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Lead / Project Manager** | 99/194 | **51.031** | 3.60 | [43.814, 57.732] | [44.330, 58.763] | [44.045, 57.977] | 0.683 | **1.000** |
| 2 | **Data Scientist** | 95/194 | **48.969** | 3.57 | [42.268, 56.186] | [41.753, 55.670] | [42.023, 55.955] | 0.317 | **1.000** |
| 3 | Business Analyst | 50/194 | 25.773 | 3.16 | [19.588, 31.959] | [20.619, 32.990] | [20.131, 32.356] | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 4 | Developer | 37/194 | 19.072 | 2.81 | [13.918, 24.742] | [13.402, 24.742] | [14.165, 25.180] | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 5 | Solution Architect | 24/194 | 12.371 | 2.34 | [7.732, 17.010] | [7.732, 17.010] | [8.456, 17.748] | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 6 | Requirements Engineer | 20/194 | 10.309 | 2.18 | [6.186, 14.948] | [6.701, 15.464] | [6.773, 15.387] | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| 7 | Other (free text) | 19/194 | 9.794 | 2.14 | [5.670, 14.433] | [5.670, 13.918] | [6.360, 14.789] | n/a (excluded from named-role ranking) | n/a |
| 8 | Test Manager / Tester | 2/194 | 1.031 | 0.73 | [0.000, 2.577] | [0.000, 2.577] | [0.283, 3.680] | 0.000 | 0.000 |

Method per your rulings: respondent-level nonparametric bootstrap, B = 10,000, seed 20261024, resampling rows with replacement; percentile CI primary, BCa (bias-correction + jackknife acceleration) and Wilson as cross-checks — all three agree to <1 pp. "-77" = non-exposure (out of denominator); the 6 Suspended rows with valid Q8 kept.

**Ordering evidence:** paired bootstrap P(Project Lead > Data Scientist) = 0.683 (they are statistically tied; difference 2.03 pp, 95% CI [−7.73, +11.34] pp), but **P(both occupy the top two) = 1.000 in all 10,000 replicates**; paired gap "min of top-2 (Data Scientist) − 3rd (Business Analyst)" = 23.19 pp, 95% CI [13.40, 32.47] pp; P(Data Scientist > Business Analyst) = 0.9999. So the identity of the top-two roles is stable, while the ordering *within* the pair is not resolvable at n = 194.

## Sensitivity grid (reported, not promoted)
| analysis set | n | Project Lead | Data Scientist | BA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRIMARY valid Q8 | 194 | 51.031 (99) | 48.969 (95) | 25.773 (50) |
| Completed + Completed-after-break | 188 | 51.064 (96) | 49.468 (93) | 26.596 (50) |
| respondents naming ≥1 role | 164 | **60.366** (99) | 57.927 (95) | 30.488 (50) |
| non-sentinel `D4_Role` ('0' = missing) | 180 | 54.444 (98) | 52.222 (94) | 25.556 (50) |
| named `D4_Role` categories only | 139 | 56.115 (78) | 53.957 (75) | 25.490 (39) |
| `-77` counted as "no" (inappropriate) | 276 | 35.870 (99) | 34.420 (95) | 18.116 (50) |

The last row shows why counting non-exposure as "no" is wrong (deflates every role ~15 pp without any information gain). The n = 164 variant is the closest defensible route to the published 61.389% (60.37% for Project Lead) — kept as sensitivity only. Blind search over every multi-select item × analysis set for ~61.4% returns only off-target, non-role items: Q11_ML_NFRs_Data_Quality = 119/194 = 61.340% and Q12_Customer_Expectations = 117/194 = 60.309% — explicitly rejected as matches, since neither is a role.

## CI-reproducibility limitation (stated, not engineered away)
Our respondent-level half-widths are ≈ ±7.0 pp at n = 194 (±2.7 pp even if one illegitimately treated the 1,358 respondent×role cells as independent). The published half-widths (0.381 pp around 49.6%, 0.434 pp around 61.389%) imply an effective n ≈ 66,154 and ≈ 48,453 respectively — two orders of magnitude above this survey. No honest denominator here can produce them; I did not rescale, subset, or re-weight to chase them.

## Corroboration only (context, not target quantities)
`D4_Role`: Data Scientist 84 (30.4%), Other 62 (22.5%), Project Lead/PM 47 (17.0%), Developer 27, unanswered "0" 23, Solution Architect 18, Business Analyst 11, Tester 2, Requirements Engineer 2 — the two roles that dominate respondents' own roles are the same two that dominate Q8 attribution. Q9 elicitation: Interviews 50.0%, Scenarios 38.7%, Prototyping 38.7%, Workshops 38.1%, Observation 33.0%. Q10 documentation: Notebooks 34.0%, User Stories 32.5%, Requirements Lists 26.3%, Prototypes 21.6%, Use-Case Models 19.6%, "Not Documented" 15.5%, BDD Scenarios 2.1% — i.e. requirements work is real but informal/ad-hoc, consistent with it being carried by leads and data scientists rather than by Requirements Engineers (10.3%) or Testers (1.0%).

Sentinel-handling log (29 entries) is in `output/sentinel_log.csv`: −99 8,776 cells/57 cols; −77 6,727 cells/83 cols; −66 3,134 cells/43 cols; "0" 763 cells overall, of which 408 in 20 categorical columns recoded to missing; 19 empty cells; 31 Duration = −1.

## Final hypothesis (submission text)
"Project Lead / Project Manager and Data Scientist are the two roles most strongly associated with requirements work in ML-enabled systems. In the survey, respondents named these two roles as the roles addressing ML/requirements aspects far more often than any other role — 51.0% (99/194; bootstrap 95% CI 43.8–57.7 percentile, 44.3–58.8 BCa, 44.0–58.0 Wilson) for Project Lead / Project Manager and 49.0% (95/194; CI 42.3–56.2 percentile, 41.8–55.7 BCa, 42.0–56.0 Wilson) for Data Scientist, versus only 25.8% for the third-ranked Business Analyst; across 10,000 seeded respondent-level bootstrap replicates these two roles occupy the top two positions in 100% of replicates (paired gap over the third role 23.2 pp, 95% CI 13.4–32.5 pp), even though their ordering within the pair is statistically indistinguishable (difference 2.0 pp, 95% CI −7.7 to +11.3 pp). We read the question's 49.6% and 61.389% pair as referring to these same two roles computed on a slightly different analysis set or publication-stage cleaning of this survey: 49.6% sits exactly in our Project-Lead/Data-Scientist range (51.0%/49.0%, or 49.5% on completed-only rows), and 61.389% is closely matched by the defensible 'respondents who named at least one role' denominator (n = 164: 60.4% Project Lead / 57.9% Data Scientist), whereas the only numeric coincidences elsewhere in the file are off-target non-role items (Q11 data-quality NFR 61.3%), which we reject. We flag as an explicit limitation that the published 95% intervals (half-widths 0.381/0.434 pp, implying an effective sample of roughly 48,000–66,000) cannot be reproduced from this extract: our honest intervals are ≈ ±7 pp at n = 194; the reproducible claim is the identity and dominance of the two roles, not the point/interval magnitudes. Substantively, requirements responsibility in ML-enabled projects is concentrated in the project-management and data-science functions, while the classic RE roles barely appear (Requirements Engineer 10.3%, Tester 1.0%), and this happens alongside documentation practices that remain ad hoc (Notebooks 34.0%, User Stories 32.5%, Requirements Lists 26.3%, and 15.5% reporting ML aspects are not documented at all)."

payload.hypothesis: Project Lead / Project Manager and Data Scientist are the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems. In the Q8_ML_Addressing_* multi-select block (Qualtrics 'quoted' = selected), 51.0% of the 194 respondents with a valid Q8 block named Project Lead / Project Manager (99/194; bootstrap 95% CI 43.8-57.7 percentile, 44.3-58.8 BCa, 44.0-58.0 Wilson) and 49.0% named Data Scientist (95/194; CI 42.3-56.2 percentile, 41.8-55.7 BCa, 42.0-56.0 Wilson), versus 25.8% for the third-ranked Business Analyst; across 10,000 seeded respondent-level bootstrap replicates these two roles take the top two spots in 100% of replicates (gap over the third role 23.2 pp, 95% CI 13.4-32.5), although their order within the pair is statistically indistinguishable (2.0 pp difference, 95% CI -7.7 to +11.3). The question's 49.6%/61.389% pair is most plausibly the same two roles computed on a slightly different analysis set or publication cleaning: 49.6% falls inside our 49.0-51.0% band, and the 'respondents naming at least one role' denominator (n=164) yields 60.4% for Project Lead; the only coincidental 61.3-61.4% values elsewhere in the file are non-role items (Q11 data-quality NFR = 61.3%) and are rejected as matches. Limitation: the published 95% intervals (half-widths 0.381/0.434 pp, implying effective n of about 48,000-66,000) cannot be reproduced from this 276-row survey - our honest intervals are about +/-7 pp at n=194 - so the reproducible claim is the identity and dominance of these two roles, not the exact point/interval magnitudes. Interpretation: responsibility for requirements in ML-enabled systems is concentrated in project management and data science rather than in the traditional requirements-engineering (10.3%) or testing (1.0%) roles, alongside ad-hoc documentation practices (Notebooks 34.0%, User Stories 32.5%, Requirements Lists 26.3%, and 15.5% reporting ML aspects are not documented).
payload.workflow: 1) Read CSV as strings to preserve sentinel codes; logged all negative/zero/blank sentinels (-99 free-text absent, -77 block not shown, -66 non-response, '0' unanswered categorical, '' empty, Duration -1). 2) Verified Q8_* (and D10, D12-D15, Q9-Q17) are multi-select 'quoted'/'not quoted' columns, not Likert, so no positivity threshold. 3) Recoded -77/-99/-66/'' to missing and '0' to missing in 20 categorical columns; analysis set = 194 respondents with a complete valid Q8 block (82 non-exposed rows excluded; 6 Suspended rows with valid Q8 kept). 4) Computed per-role proportions with 10,000-replicate seeded (20261024) respondent-level bootstrap: percentile CI, BCa (bias correction + jackknife acceleration) and Wilson analytic cross-check; bootstrap SE ~2-3.6 pp. 5) Computed bootstrap rank-1/rank-2/top-2 probabilities over the 7 named roles plus paired bootstrap contrasts (PL-DS, DS-BA). 6) Ran sensitivity grid (completed-only, naming>=1 role, non-sentinel D4_Role, named D4_Role only, and the inappropriate -77-as-'no' variant). 7) Diagnosed CI reproducibility (implied effective n from published half-widths) and blind-searched every multi-select item for ~61.4% to test the second published value. 8) Wrote per-role, sensitivity, sentinel-log, diagnostics, corroboration and search tables to output/, plus bootstrap distributions and run metadata. Determinism checked by re-running and comparing checksums.
